rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No combative verbs about the agent in body prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest is 39, 'Push back on the five.' - push back is directed at the agent's proposals, sits in the steer/ask family, and is the training's own house verb for review-moved-upstream. No bark/order/command/whip/boss verbs in lines 1-65.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't state a count the adjacent list already holds.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 39: 'Push back on the five.' - the numeral names an output the agent produced in the prompt above, not items visible as an adjacent bullet list, so it is the memory-handle carve-out rather than a tally.

findings.quote: This is crucially the step that changes how the run behaves.
findings.harm: Banned consultancy adverb; it flinches the engineer reader and the rule is zero-tolerance grep. Present here, one body hit, view.json greps.banned_words body_hits 1.

findings.quote: Treat this as a ritual you repeat at the start of every session.
findings.harm: Ritual imports the Scrum-ceremony register the training exists to replace, and it teaches the student to file this beat as recurring theatre. Present, one body hit.
findings.fix: Cut the sentence, or say 'a move you can repeat' - and only if the claim is true, which for a one-off close-out it is not.

findings.quote: This section previously said something different; it was fixed on 2026-01-14.
findings.harm: Changelog in a student-facing body. A reader who never saw the old version loses nothing, and the sentence goes stale on every later edit while still reading fine. Present, and it carries both tells: transition verb 'previously' and a bare date.

findings.quote: At this point the student should notice the test is still red.
findings.harm: Third-person plus trainer delivery mechanics in body prose; the student reads about themselves in the third person and the room-cue reaches the wrong audience. Present.
findings.fix: Move the cue below the maintainer cut, or recast in second person. It also contradicts line 62, which says the failing-test loop closed.

findings.quote: There is no penalty if you skip this, and it is completely fine either way.
findings.harm: Reassurance-shaped sentence; a senior reader registers that the author thought the beat needed defending. Present - 'no penalty' is a listed flag phrase verbatim.
findings.fix: Cut it. Line 39 already frames the optional push-back as gain, not obligation.

findings.quote: Anything can be inspected and reverse-engineered with an LLM
findings.harm: The slogan lands with no boundary downstream, so a student takes 'anything' at face value and applies the move to a tracker with no field discipline. The backing stance at line 134 states the caveat lives in a third bullet of this section; the section has two bullets and no caveat, so the boundary is missing rather than deliberately placed.
findings.fix: Add one Boris-direct carve-out sentence after the slogan naming what the read depends on, and bring the backing keep-note back into step with what the body actually says.

findings.quote: the step that changes how the run behaves
findings.harm: Noun-run for the agent's sitting collides with the reserved sense (test/CI/eval executions), which is exactly the split the vocabulary registry exists to keep clean. Present, though mild - the sentence is going anyway under rule 1.
findings.fix: 'how the session goes', or name the task.
